title: Hysteresis + probe noise led to underscaling during a bursty cold-start (postmortem)
creator: Riley Morgan
description: During a production traffic spike on 2025-02-17 we observed a period of sustained high tail latency and elevated 5xxs for a subset of inference routes. The immediate mitigation restored capacity, but analysis showed HPA/KEDA configuration interacting with probe noise and cold-start latency produced sustained underscaling during the burst window. This document summarizes timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action items.
timeline:
2025-02-17 09:45 UTC - Traffic spike begins for /v1/generate routes (client A ramp test).
2025-02-17 09:47 UTC - SRE alerts: 95th percentile latency > 800ms and 5xx rate increase.
2025-02-17 09:49 UTC - Automated fallback to a lower-cost model activated for affected tenants.
2025-02-17 09:50 UTC - Manual scale-up request executed (increase pool target replicas).
2025-02-17 10:05 UTC - Latency returns to baseline after extra capacity and warm pool activation.
2025-02-18 - Deep-dive started with serving/runtime and platform teams.
2025-02-25 - Root-cause hypothesis validated in staging with traffic replay.
2025-03-03 - Configuration changes and PRs merged; controlled canary rollout completed.
detection: Alerting triggered on latency SLO breach and elevated 5xx. Initial dashboards suggested normal cluster CPU metrics, causing confusion. Further investigation of scaler telemetry and Prometheus scrape intervals revealed noisy target metric sampling around the spike onset which hid the actual queue-depth increase from the scaler for several scrape windows.
impact: Approximately 17 minutes of degraded latency for 4% of production requests on a subset of routes behind a particular model variant during the spike window. No persistent data loss. Some customers experienced higher tail latency and transient 5xxs; most recovered after routing fallback and manual scale-up.
root_cause: Multiple contributing factors combined to produce an underscaling regression: 1) KEDA Prometheus scaler used a raw per-replica latency metric (p95_latency) that had high short-term variance; 2) Prometheus scrape interval (30s) + KEDA polling introduced aliasing so KEDA saw a smoothed/attenuated signal for ~60-90s after spike onset; 3) HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds and KEDA cooldown settings were too short for our cold-start characteristics leading to premature scale-down decisions immediately prior to the spike; 4) Pod readiness probe initialDelay and model warm-up time caused new replicas to be unready for longer than KEDA/HPA expected, reducing effective capacity even as replicas were created; 5) No warm standby pool for certain dedicated capacity tiers, so cold-start cost was high and scaling decisions needed to account for it.
mitigation:
Short-term: 1) Enabled a temporary routing fallback to alternate model variants for affected tenants during high spike alerts (rolled back after stable). 2) Increased KEDA polling frequency to reduce detection latency for the specific Prometheus scaler (from 60s to 20s) in the affected clusters. 3) Temporarily increased HPA minReplicas for critical model routes to ensure headroom.
Medium-term: 1) Adjusted readiness probe initialDelaySeconds and added a model-warm readiness check to avoid marking pods Ready before the model is usable. 2) Updated Prometheus exporter to provide a more stable scaling metric (request_queue_depth) computed as a moving-average and exposed at 10s resolution. 3) Tuned HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to 120s and KEDA cooldown to 90s to add hysteresis.
Long-term: Implement warm pool for model nodes and change default autoscaler config to use the new queue-based metric and smoothing window.
long_term_fix: 1) Implement node-level warm pool (pre-warmed replicas) for high-cost model families; integrate warm pool awareness into rollout/placement algorithms. 2) Replace per-pod noisy latency metric with cluster-level request_queue_depth moving average as primary autoscaling signal for inference groups. 3) Add adaptive hysteresis: when a cold-start penalty is detected, increase stabilizationWindow and temporarily bias scaling towards scale-up. 4) Build an autoscale test harness (synthetic bursts) in CI that validates HPA/KEDA reactions under realistic cold-start latencies. 5) Document recommended scaler metrics and platform defaults in runtime-ops runbook.
